title: Colony Wars
subtitle: A pilot inside a larger war

body: Colony Wars is Psygnosis's 1997 PlayStation space-combat game, first released in North America on 4 November. The League of Free Worlds fights an Earth empire that draws resources from its colonies. The player enters that struggle as a pilot, flying the craft assigned to each mission rather than controlling the whole war. Battles range across space with fighters, larger vessels and specific objectives. Success matters, but the campaign also accommodates failure, allowing the story to continue along a different route instead of always demanding that an unsuccessful mission be repeated.

High Command selects the starfighter, giving each mission a particular combination of weapons and capabilities. Energy weapons, missiles and torpedoes answer different targets; some craft also carry nonlethal EMP cannons. Countermeasures help escape incoming missiles, while a grapple gun can secure important objects. The player must read the assigned equipment alongside the objective. A mission is therefore more than clearing everything from the view: the available weapons help define what should be destroyed, disabled or recovered, and which threats have to be survived while that work is completed.

Missions are grouped into acts, with performance directing the campaign through branching paths. Certain encounters become turning points, so a lost engagement need not end the war or produce the same outcome as another defeat. Combat records let the player review the service already completed. A voiced database describes ships and planets, supplying context beyond the immediate cockpit view. Tim Wright composed the score. Colony Wars: Vengeance followed in 1998 and Red Sun in 2000, extending a series that gave PlayStation players both space battles and a campaign shaped by their results.
